# Native builtin source admission

This is the immutable source-storage component for the planned upstream Node
embedding. It does not execute JavaScript or replace upstream's module loader.
`BuiltinSourceView` borrows read-only storage for the program lifetime. Exact
ID lookup, including embedded NULs, uses `std::string_view` lengths.

Source classification and wrapper argument lists come from the original,
unmodified `upstream/src/builtin_info.cc` and `builtin_info.h`. The build-time
`nodejs-builtin-metadata` tool executes that code. It emits logical source
metadata only; no host layouts, process state or capabilities are used to
describe the guest. This original C++ implementation needs C++20; the registry
consumer itself needs C++17. Keeping classification at build time also avoids
unchecked C++ string/map allocations in guest compiler entrypoints.

Generate the private build include through declared development tools:

```sh
# NODE_REGISTRY_WORK is a new, task-owned build directory.
clang++ -std=c++20 \
  -I third_party/nodejs/upstream/src \
  scripts/nodejs-builtin-metadata.cpp \
  third_party/nodejs/upstream/src/builtin_info.cc \
  -o "$NODE_REGISTRY_WORK/nodejs-builtin-metadata"
python3 scripts/generate-nodejs-source-registry.py \
  --manifest third_party/nodejs/sources.json \
  --metadata-tool "$NODE_REGISTRY_WORK/nodejs-builtin-metadata" \
  --output "$NODE_REGISTRY_WORK/node-source-registry.generated.inc"
```

The generator verifies builtin byte lengths/hashes and the original metadata
source hashes before emitting. It records source-manifest, metadata-tool and
metadata-source hashes, verifies the metadata protocol and atomically publishes
only after input admission. Generated byte storage is a disposable build output,
not checked-in generated JavaScript or a rewritten algorithm. The original
JavaScript source files remain unchanged.

Compile `builtin-source-registry.cpp` with this directory and the generated
include directory on its include path. The API enumerates the immutable source
records and returns exact ID matches. Kinds, parameter names and diagnostic
origins are admitted metadata; compilation and execution remain separate.

`tests/nodejs/upstream/source-registry-controls.cpp` reads all admitted bytes
and metadata through the actual compiled C++ lookup API. It includes missing-ID,
out-of-bounds and embedded-NUL lookup controls. Its framed output must be
compared to the source manifest and independently reviewed source registration;
a successful process exit by itself is insufficient.

The SpiderMonkey-specific compiler consumer is under
`packages/registry/spidermonkey/node-upstream/`. The source recipe now stages/registers it in the Mozilla shell build.
It has not been compiled against the guest engine or exercised as a guest.
